channel.title: Updated · all tabs
channel.description: Daily news and research, explained: every tab

item.title: Hera's first close-ups show DART left a stadium-sized crater and a tumbling asteroid surrounded by boulders
item.description: ESA's Hera spacecraft has returned the first close images of Dimorphos, showing that NASA's 2022 DART impact carved a crater nearly as wide as the asteroid and left it tumbling. (CNN, Ars Technica)

item.title: Niobium phosphide wires a few nanometres wide conduct better as they shrink, the opposite of copper
item.description: A Stanford-led study in Nature reports that ribbons of the semimetal niobium phosphide only 5 to 6 nanometres wide become less resistive as they narrow, unlike copper chip wiring. (Tech Xplore (Stanford University release), Nature)

item.title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage
item.description: Draining peatlands since 1800 accounts for about 2.7% of today's human-caused warming influence, and the effect could nearly double by 2100 even if no more peatland is drained. (Jevan B. Yu, Etienne Fluet-Chouinard, Susan E. Page et al. · Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Pacific Northwest National Laboratory; University of Leicester; UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology)

item.title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains
item.description: Delft physicists coupled two minimal Kitaev chains in a nanowire and observed coherent oscillations of fermion parity, which they describe as the first coherent control of a Majorana qubit. (Francesco Zatelli, Bart Roovers, Nick van Loo et al. · Delft University of Technology)

item.title: US proposes new Section 301 tariffs on China, the EU and 12 other trading partners over excess factory capacity
item.description: The Trump administration proposed new tariffs on 14 economies, including an additional 20% on Chinese goods, to replace import taxes the Supreme Court struck down in February. (The Globe and Mail, BBC, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: US PCE inflation holds at 3.8% in October and core inflation reaches 3.3%, as real consumer spending slips
item.description: The Federal Reserve's preferred price index rose 3.8% in the year to October, and 3.3% excluding food and energy, slightly above the 3.2% core rate economists expected. (Bureau of Economic Analysis, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: US third-quarter GDP growth is revised up to 4.3%, the fastest pace in three years
item.description: The US economy grew at a 4.3% annual rate in the third quarter, not 3.4% as first estimated, after upgrades to software investment and consumer spending. (Bureau of Economic Analysis, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Norse Atlantic suspends its flights and says it will file for bankruptcy unless it finds funding urgently
item.description: The Norwegian long-haul budget airline cancelled Thursday's flights a day after its shares fell 85%, and says it is in takeover talks with investors. (RTE, Euronews)

item.title: UK discount chain Poundland collapses into administration, putting 11,000 jobs and 600 shops at risk
item.description: Poundland's US owner, Gordon Brothers, put the retailer into administration after sale talks failed; shops stay open while administrators AlixPartners seek buyers for all or parts of it. (BBC, Euronews, BBC)

item.title: Democratizing Venture Capital: Tax Incentives and the Geographic Expansion of Startup Investing
item.description: Removing federal capital gains tax on qualifying startup stock in 2009–2010 raised the chance that a metro area with no venture capital received its first investment by 8 to 10 percentage points. (Murillo Campello, Guilherme Junqueira)

item.title: Nvidia reportedly halts server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries after new US chip export rule
item.description: The Financial Times reports that Nvidia told server makers to stop shipping to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after a US rule made advanced-chip exports to those countries subject to licences. (The Star (Reuters), Al Jazeera)

item.title: 42 state attorneys general move to stop bankrupt Character.AI from auctioning users' private chats
item.description: A bipartisan coalition of 42 attorneys general is intervening in Character.AI's bankruptcy to block a 1 December auction of chat histories from more than 21 million US accounts. (TechCrunch, The Verge)

item.title: Reinforcement Learning Can Be Recovered From Its Own Rollouts
item.description: Plain supervised fine-tuning on the saved rollouts of a reinforcement learning run, in order and without reward labels, reproduces the run's learning curve, and one late batch can recover its final score. (Jiayi Sheng, Jingwen Gu, Guanning Zeng et al. · Carnegie Mellon University, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Harvard University)

item.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
item.description: The Mixture-of-Loops Transformer passes attention keys and values between loops instead of only the residual stream, so a looped model can decode each new token in a single pass. (Lianghui Zhu, Shijie Wang, Xinggang Wang et al. · Huazhong University of Science & Technology, ByteDance Seed, University of Toronto)

item.title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments
item.description: OmniAct trains one 400M-parameter manipulation policy on about a million procedurally generated robot arms, feeding it each robot's joint geometry in camera coordinates so it can control bodies it has never seen. (Xiang Fan, Yuheng Wang, Jiayuan Yan et al. · University of Washington, Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill)

item.title: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe
item.description: Agents often answer while their own stated belief still lists several possibilities; rewarding each step against the simulator's exact posterior teaches them to keep gathering evidence until it settles the answer. (Richmond Sin Jing Xuan, Peilin Feng, Wenbin Wang et al. · Nanyang Technological University)

item.title: ThinkMorph-SSL: Scaling Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning with Pretext Tasks
item.description: ThinkMorph-SSL turns classic self-supervised image tasks such as jigsaw and denoising into practice for models that reason by generating intermediate images, raising accuracy by 11.33 points across twelve benchmarks. (Jiawei Gu, Linjie Li, Yiming Liu et al. · University of Washington, Tsinghua University, Zhejiang University)

item.title: 1Password says an attacker used an employee's GitHub account to steal customer names and emails, but not password vaults
item.description: 1Password disclosed that an attacker who took over an employee's GitHub account planted code in its backend and downloaded customer account records, while password vaults and their encryption keys stayed out of reach. (TechCrunch, BleepingComputer)

item.title: The FCC conditionally authorizes SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites as orbital data centers
item.description: The FCC gave SpaceX conditional approval for a constellation of up to 1 million data-center satellites, with 14 years to deploy it, while withholding a waiver on how retired satellites are disposed of. (Ars Technica, TechCrunch)

item.title: Palo Alto Networks confirms attackers are exploiting the Fragnesia Linux flaw on firewalls with internet-exposed management interfaces
item.description: Palo Alto Networks says attackers are chaining a PHP flaw with the Fragnesia Linux kernel flaw against PAN-OS firewalls whose management interface faces the internet, and has released fixes. (BleepingComputer, Palo Alto Networks)

item.title: Drupal confirms attackers are exploiting a highly critical installer flaw to take over unpatched websites
item.description: Drupal says an installer flaw patched on November 18 has been exploited on live sites since November 19; CISA ordered US federal agencies to fix it by Friday. (BleepingComputer, Drupal.org)

item.title: Reducing RSA-2048 Factoring Resources Below One Billion Toffolis via LLM-Driven Verifiable Quantum Compilation
item.description: A redesigned circuit for factoring 2048-bit RSA numbers on a quantum computer needs fewer than one billion Toffoli gates, down from billions, at roughly 1,300 to 2,900 logical qubits. (Xiaodi Li, Yuqing Wang, Xue Chen et al. · Intelligent Quantum Inception Co., Ltd. ; Tsinghua University)

item.title: FDA approves bezuclastinib with sunitinib for gastrointestinal stromal tumours after imatinib
item.description: The FDA approved Cogent's Ekitna (bezuclastinib) with sunitinib for advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumours after imatinib; in a phase 3 trial the pair held the cancer in check for a median 16.5 months versus 9.2. (Cogent Biosciences (GlobeNewswire release, via WBOC), Pharmaceutical Technology)

item.title: England records 5,258 heat-associated deaths in 2026, the most since monitoring began
item.description: The UK Health Security Agency estimates 5,258 deaths in England were associated with heat between May and September 2026, far above the previous record of 2,985 in 2022. (The Guardian, BBC)

item.title: Dolphins with larger, more predictable social groups live longer, a 40-year study in Shark Bay finds
item.description: Four decades of observations of about 400 wild bottlenose dolphins show that animals that are more sociable and more consistent in the group sizes they keep tend to live longer. (PLOS Biology, University of Queensland, The Guardian)

item.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
item.description: In 9,476 Brazilians with type 2 diabetes, aiming for systolic blood pressure below 120 instead of below 140 mm Hg did not significantly cut cardiovascular events, and kidney-function declines were more frequent. (Karla Santo Eduardo Martins Gisele S. Silva Patricia O. Guimarães Caio A.M. Tavares João B. Andrade Frederico Monfardini Josué Nieri Silvia R.L. Assis João S. Felício Fábio S. Silveira Marcos S. item.title: A shared meaning component across languages in the human brain
item.description: Models trained to predict brain responses to one language also predict responses to languages they never saw, across speakers of 21 languages, pointing to a shared representation of meaning. (Andrea Gregor de Varda, Saima Malik-Moraleda, Greta Tuckute et al. · McGovern Institute for Brain Research and Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences, MIT)

item.title: Architecture of the poxvirus early-transcription machinery and portal complex
item.description: Imaging of intact vaccinia virus cores shows the virus's gene-copying enzymes parked in pairs beside the genome, next to a channel through the core wall suited to exporting RNA. (Benoît Arragain, Lukas W. Bauer, Victor-Valentin Hodirnau et al. · Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA))

item.title: China launches Shenzhou-24 with a Pakistani astronaut, the first foreigner to fly on a Chinese crewed mission
item.description: Shenzhou-24 carried two Chinese astronauts and Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali to the Tiangong space station, the first time a foreign crew member has flown in China's crewed programme. (BBC News, Phys.org (Associated Press))

item.title: NOAA closes a hurricane season split by El Niño: one Atlantic hurricane, record activity in the eastern Pacific
item.description: NOAA's end-of-season summary counts 10 Atlantic named storms and a single hurricane, against 20 named storms and eight major hurricanes in the eastern Pacific, a contrast it attributes to a very strong El Niño. (Phys.org (NOAA release), iHeart)

item.title: Interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer for low-loss soft ultrasonic interfaces
item.description: A dry, stretchy rubber built entirely from bottlebrush-shaped polymers transmits ultrasound efficiently without any gel and kept a wearable imager working for about nine days. (Shu Wang, Runze Li, Zihan Tang et al. · MIT; Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology; University of Wisconsin at Madison; National University of Singapore; Nanyang Technological University)

item.title: Small and large earthquakes driven by inelastic deformation in weak fault zones
item.description: An earthquake-cycle model that lets the rock around a fault deform permanently reproduces both small and large earthquakes, and suggests that fault zones can be mechanically very weak. (Peng Zhai, Yihe Huang, Jean-Paul Ampuero · University of Michigan)

item.title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
item.description: Pretreating the electrode of a perovskite solar cell so its molecular contact layer bonds at several points gives 27.3% efficiency and 94% retention after 400 cycles between -40 and 85 °C. (Jiaxin Wu, Hongzhuo Wu, Zuhong Zhang et al.)

item.title: Britain's energy price cap will rise 26% in January, taking a typical annual bill to £2,166
item.description: Ofgem will lift the cap on default energy tariffs by 26% from 1 January after wholesale gas prices surged, affecting around 20 million households in England, Scotland and Wales. (Ofgem, BBC)

item.title: Bank of Canada will stress headline inflation and may raise rates sooner when supply shocks hit
item.description: Governor Tiff Macklem set out how the renewed 2% inflation framework will work in practice: more weight on headline CPI, new preferred core measures and a readiness to act early on large supply shocks. (Bank of Canada, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Dell's quarterly revenue doubles to $54.9 billion as its AI server backlog reaches $132 billion
item.description: Dell reported record third-quarter revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103%, raised its full-year revenue guidance to $202 billion and added $25 billion to its share buyback authorization. (Dell Technologies, BigGo Finance)

item.title: Subprime used-car dealer America's Car-Mart files for Chapter 11 and agrees to sell itself to a group led by former executives
item.description: America's Car-Mart filed a pre-packaged Chapter 11 case in Texas with $60 million of new financing and a deal to sell substantially all its assets to Cardinal Asset Holdings. (Yahoo Finance, Car Dealership Guy News)

item.title: CFOs Meet LLMs
item.description: An AI model asked to role-play individual chief financial officers predicted their actual survey answers on economic optimism, explaining 27% of the variation across 6,075 responses from 2002 to 2025. (John R. Graham, Campbell R. Harvey, Manish Jha · Duke University; NBER; Georgia State University)

item.title: Z.ai releases GLM-5.4, a 750B-scale flagship that runs 28 shared layers twice per forward pass
item.description: Chinese lab Z.ai released GLM-5.4, its first flagship built as a looped transformer, available only in its own products for now, with open weights promised after safety hardening. (Z.ai developer docs, Simon Willison, MarkTechPost)

item.title: Anthropic shares fall below their $83 IPO price less than a week after the record listing
item.description: Anthropic's stock dropped below its $83 offer price on Tuesday, trading near $76 at midday, as a broad technology selloff erased the premium from its Nasdaq debut. (The Globe and Mail, TechCrunch)

item.title: Can Latent Reasoning Drive LLM Outputs Without a Trace?
item.description: A fine-tuned model can run a multi-step hidden rule entirely in its activations, then write chain-of-thought that justifies the result without mentioning the rule, and a frontier LLM monitor does not flag it. (Tomer Ashuach, Zorik Gekhman, Avi Caciularu et al. · Technion – Israel Institute of Technology, Google Research)

item.title: Recursive Collective Intelligence: Emergence on an Equal-Budget Ladder in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
item.description: Judged at equal token cost, agent teams beat independent agents only when they move facts no single agent holds, and such teams can train their successors on their own verified work. (Lixuan He, Shengqu Cai, Fang Wu et al.)

item.title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
item.description: Loom attention lets each attention head choose, per token, which earlier heads it reads from, and a 2.8B model built this way matches a 12B Pythia baseline for about 2% extra compute. (Da Xiao, Qingye Meng, Shengping Li et al. · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, ColorfulClouds Technology)

item.title: Verifiable On-Policy Distillation
item.description: VOPD uses the agreement between a verifier and a teacher model on sampled answers to strengthen or reverse the teacher's token-level guidance, giving dense training signal that is tied to checked outcomes. (Juntong Shi, Stefano Ermon, Jure Leskovec et al. · Stanford University, Google DeepMind)

item.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
item.description: A controlled study of how to wrap a frontier multimodal model as a robot policy reaches 83.3% on RoboLab-120 and finds the model succeeds through spatial target estimation, not low-level motion skill. (Xiao-Ming Wu, Kang Liao, Yuexiao Ma et al. · Nanyang Technological University, ACE Robotics, SenseTime Research)

item.title: Hackers reportedly breach an unclassified intelligence analysis system used by the CIA and two other US spy agencies
item.description: Unknown attackers reportedly broke into an open-source intelligence system at the CIA, also affecting ODNI and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency; a source says no classified networks or data were involved. (BleepingComputer, The Verge, The Record)

item.title: The US Treasury's financial crimes bureau FinCEN takes systems offline after unauthorized access
item.description: FinCEN, the Treasury bureau that receives banks' suspicious-activity reports, says intruders accessed a limited subset of its systems; it took some systems offline and extended filing deadlines. (The Verge, The Record, BleepingComputer)

item.title: A US jury convicts Huawei on 10 of 12 counts, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets, bank fraud and sanctions violations
item.description: A federal jury in New York found Huawei and three subsidiaries guilty of stealing US companies' technology, defrauding banks and violating Iran sanctions, but acquitted it of racketeering; sentencing is set for September 2027. (The Verge, The Register)

item.title: Microsoft declares an internal "Code Red" after its November email outage and sets a one-hour target for resolving major incidents
item.description: Internal memos reviewed by Reuters show Microsoft has made reliability work on Microsoft 365 its top engineering priority after the November 12 outage, which a senior executive called the worst in Exchange Online's history. (Ars Technica, The Verge)

item.title: Aftershock: Yesterday's Linux Kernel Bugs, Tomorrow's Android Exploits
item.description: An automated pipeline using an off-the-shelf language model turned public Linux kernel fixes into 17 verified Android privilege-escalation exploits, while the same fixes took a median of 181 days to reach Pixel phones. (Kareem Shehada, Zhiyun Qian · University of California, Riverside)

item.title: FDA approves giredestrant after surgery, the first new hormone therapy for early-stage breast cancer in over 20 years
item.description: The FDA approved Roche's daily pill Wilserdly for early breast cancer after surgery, on the strength of a 4,170-patient trial in which it cut recurrence or death by 30% against standard hormone therapy. (FDA, Fierce Pharma)

item.title: FDA approves ribitol, the first treatment for any form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy
item.description: The FDA approved Welgemda, a twice-daily oral solution, for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 after a 112-patient placebo-controlled trial showed gains in walking speed and lung function at 12 months. (FDA, STAT)

item.title: Kymera's once-daily eczema pill cuts disease severity by 72% in a 244-patient mid-stage trial, the company reports
item.description: In a randomized phase 2b trial, an oral drug that destroys the immune signalling protein STAT6 reduced eczema severity scores by 72% against 27% on placebo; the results are company-reported, not yet peer-reviewed. (Kymera Therapeutics press release (via BioSpace), New Scientist, Dermatology Times)

item.title: CMR to Guide Defibrillator Implantation for LVEF
item.description: In a randomized trial of 353 patients with moderately reduced heart function and scarring on cardiac MRI, implanted defibrillators did not significantly reduce sudden cardiac death or serious arrhythmia over 6.3 years. (Joseph B. Selvanayagam, et al. (CMR GUIDE Investigators) · Flinders University and Flinders Medical Centre, Adelaide)

item.title: A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control
item.description: An implant that runs on the body's own glucose stimulated the vagus nerve whenever its fuel-cell voltage signalled high blood sugar, and lowered blood glucose in diabetic rats over weeks. (Weijun Xiu, Qian Wang, Ling Wan et al. · National University of Singapore)

item.title: Euclid finds the most distant quasar yet, a 360-million-solar-mass black hole 630 million years after the Big Bang
item.description: Euclid astronomers confirmed a quasar at redshift 8.13, the first beyond 8, whose slowly feeding 360-million-solar-mass black hole strains models of how early black holes grew. (Euclid Consortium, University of Hamburg, Phys.org)

item.title: Webb's dust map of Cassiopeia A suggests the star's inner layers merged shortly before it exploded
item.description: Webb resolved the chemistry of individual dust clumps in the Cassiopeia A supernova remnant and found signs that burning shells inside the star mixed, possibly hours before the explosion. (NASA, Phys.org)

item.title: NASA asks industry to build a 20-kilowatt fission reactor for the Moon, to be ready for launch by 2030
item.description: NASA issued a request for proposals for Lunar Reactor-1, a 20-kilowatt fission system meant to be launch-ready by 2030 and to run on the Moon for at least five years. (NASA)

item.title: Quiet within, chaos without: Turbulence shelters drive selective particle capture and release
item.description: Hollow capsules with a single hole use the calm they create inside a turbulent fluid to collect particles of one chosen size and release them on demand. (Matteo Sabato, Sarah Chong, Yaocheng Li et al. · University of Chicago; New York University)

item.title: Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations
item.description: Chemists report a modular reaction that assembles benzene rings carrying six different groups, with the position of each one fixed in advance by the choice of starting materials. (Guillaume Mollaert, Hang-Fei Tu, Jacob R. King et al. · ICIQ)
